title: Supernovae: Explosion Pathways, Distance Calibration, and Element Origins
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
“Supernova” names an observed stellar explosion, not one unique mechanism. In a core-collapse supernova, a massive star develops an unstable core after successive stages of nuclear burning. Collapse, neutrino transport, shocks, and the surrounding stellar layers interact in a complex explosion. The remnant may become a neutron star or, in some cases, a black hole. The outcome depends on mass, structure, rotation, composition, and mass loss; a single initial-mass threshold cannot describe every star.

A Type Ia supernova is a thermonuclear disruption involving a carbon-oxygen white dwarf in a binary system. Possible pathways include mass transfer from a non-degenerate companion or the interaction and merger of white dwarfs. The progenitor problem remains an active field. Therefore, the simple story of one white dwarf quietly reaching exactly the same limiting mass is a useful historical model, not a complete account of all observed events.

Type Ia supernovae are valuable distance indicators because their light curves and colors contain empirical information that can be used to standardize peak luminosity. They are not perfectly identical candles before correction. Astronomers compare apparent brightness with standardized luminosity, while accounting for dust, redshift, detector calibration, sample selection, and possible population differences. Distance follows from a calibrated relation, not from the label “Type Ia” alone.

Supernovae also synthesize and disperse elements, but “we are made only by supernovae” is too simple. The Big Bang produced mainly light nuclei; stars built many heavier nuclei through fusion; stellar explosions created or expelled additional isotopes; and neutron-star mergers provide important environments for some of the heaviest elements. The origin of an element is often a distribution across processes. Cosmic history is a network of production, ejection, mixing, and later star formation—not a single furnace.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Every supernova has the same physical mechanism and brightness.

options.label: B
options.text: Supernovae require distinctions among explosion pathways, calibrated distance use, and multiple sources of elements.

options.label: C
options.text: Type Ia events are caused only by the collapse of massive stellar cores.

options.label: D
options.text: All elements heavier than helium come from one type of explosion.

questions.answer: 正解：B。本文は重力崩壊型とIa型の機構を区別し、Ia型を補正して距離指標にする過程と、元素起源が複数環境に分布することを論じます。A・C・Dはいずれも本文が退ける単純化です。

questions.prompt: Which comparison between core-collapse and Type Ia supernovae is supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Core collapse begins in the unstable core of a massive star, whereas a Type Ia event is a thermonuclear disruption involving a carbon-oxygen white dwarf in a binary system.

options.label: B
options.text: Both are necessarily caused by a white dwarf reaching exactly the same limiting mass.

options.label: C
options.text: Core collapse always leaves a white dwarf, whereas a Type Ia event always leaves a neutron star.

options.label: D
options.text: Both names identify one identical progenitor system and one identical explosion mechanism.

questions.answer: 正解：A。重力崩壊型は大質量星の不安定な中心核の崩壊を起点とし、中性子星やブラックホールを残し得ます。Ia型は連星中の炭素酸素白色矮星の熱核的破壊であり、起源経路も一つに確定していません。

questions.prompt: Which meaning is closest to “the progenitor problem remains an active field” in paragraph 2?

options.label: A
options.text: Every initial system has already been identified.

options.label: B
options.text: Researchers still test multiple origin scenarios.

options.label: C
options.text: The explosions have stopped occurring.

options.label: D
options.text: Only the names of stars are uncertain.

questions.answer: 正解：B。質量移動を伴う経路や白色矮星同士の相互作用・合体など、複数の起源シナリオが今も観測と模型で検討されているという意味です。

questions.prompt: Why can a single initial-mass threshold not determine the outcome of every massive star?

options.label: A
options.text: Because initial mass has no relationship to stellar evolution.

options.label: B
options.text: Because structure, rotation, composition, and mass loss also influence the explosion and the remnant.

options.label: C
options.text: Because every massive star undergoes a Type Ia explosion.

options.label: D
options.text: Because detector calibration changes a star's physical mass.

questions.answer: 正解：B。初期質量に加え、内部構造、回転、組成、爆発前の質量放出が中心核と外層を変え、爆発可能性や残骸を左右します。一つの境界値だけでは条件差を表せません。

questions.prompt: What does it mean to call Type Ia supernovae standardizable rather than perfectly identical candles?

options.label: A
options.text: Their intrinsic luminosities are unknowable, so astronomers use the label alone.

options.label: B
options.text: Observable light-curve and color information can correct luminosity differences and produce a calibrated comparison, although the events are not identical before correction.

options.label: C
options.text: Their apparent brightness is the same at every distance and through every amount of dust.

options.label: D
options.text: Standardization removes the need to test calibration, selection, or population effects.

questions.answer: 正解：B。最大光度が最初から同じなのではなく、光度曲線や色という観測特徴で個体差を補正し、較正された光度へ近づけます。したがって塵、装置、標本選択、母集団差の検査も必要です。

questions.prompt: Which statement about systematic error in supernova distance measurement does the passage support?

options.label: A
options.text: Classification alone gives an exact distance.

options.label: B
options.text: Dust and sample selection cannot affect supernova cosmology.

options.label: C
options.text: Light-curve correction helps, but calibration and population effects must still be tested.

options.label: D
options.text: Apparent brightness always equals intrinsic luminosity.

questions.answer: 正解：C。光度曲線と色による標準化は有用ですが、塵、赤方偏移、検出器較正、標本選択、母集団差が系統誤差になり得ます。分類名だけで正確な距離は得られません。

questions.prompt: Which list contains the four element-producing or element-supplying environments named in paragraph 4?

options.label: A
options.text: The Big Bang, fusion inside stars, stellar explosions, and neutron-star mergers

options.label: B
options.text: Only core-collapse supernovae, Type Ia supernovae, black holes, and dust

options.label: C
options.text: Redshift, detector calibration, sample selection, and apparent brightness

options.label: D
options.text: Mass transfer, rotation, sea-floor spreading, and planetary erosion

questions.answer: 正解：A。本文はビッグバン、恒星内部の核融合、超新星などの恒星爆発、中性子星合体を挙げます。それぞれが作る核種や寄与率は同じではありません。

questions.prompt: What does the sentence “The origin of an element is often a distribution across processes” imply?

options.label: A
options.text: Every element must be assigned to one dramatic event with no uncertainty.

options.label: B
options.text: Several environments may contribute to the same element or isotope, so their relative contributions and uncertainties should be tested.

options.label: C
options.text: Elements are produced only after they enter a detector.

options.label: D
options.text: Mixing and later star formation erase all evidence about element origins.

questions.answer: 正解：B。「元素の起源はしばしば複数過程にまたがる分布である」という意味です。同じ元素・同位体へ複数環境が寄与し得るため、一つの劇的原因へ固定するより寄与率と不確実性を示す方が検証可能です。

questions.prompt: Which research plan would best justify calling an astronomical object “standardizable”?

options.label: A
options.text: Test it across distance, host environment, wavelength, and instrument; calibrate predictive features; quantify residual scatter; model dust and selection; and compare with independent distance methods.

options.label: B
options.text: Assume that all objects with the same label are physically identical and ignore outliers.

options.label: C
options.text: Use apparent brightness alone and avoid reporting uncertainty or population change.

options.label: D
options.text: Choose only nearby bright examples and apply their average to every redshift without further testing.

questions.answer: 正解：A。標準化の信頼性には、予測特徴と固有光度の関係、較正方法、補正後の散らばり、塵・選択・赤方偏移・母集団変化のモデル化、独立距離法との比較が必要です。「標準」という名称だけでは根拠になりません。
